Democracy Defender Mod Manager (DDMM), release candidate 19: *your mods, your democracy, defended.* It's still an
early build, but it's meant to be usable by anyone, not just developers.

**The DDMM Promise, in brief:** every mod is welcome (DDMM never blocks, blacklists or ranks mods or mod sites),
no account is ever needed on any site, your files stay in a folder you control, it's Apache-2.0 open source
forever, and update checks never run unless you ask.

## Quick start

1. **Download** the right file for you (see the table below).
2. **Run it.** DDMM looks for your Helldivers 2 install automatically. If Steam is in its usual place, there's
   nothing to set up.
3. **Add mods and click Deploy.** Drag in an archive or folder, or click "Add URL" and paste a link.

**Works with AyakaMods, Nexus Mods, ModWorkshop, GameBanana, GitHub, any direct link, or files already on your
disk.** Special love to the AyakaMods community ❤️, one of the best homes for Helldivers 2 modding. Go say hi:
<https://ayakamods.com/games/helldivers-2.119/>.

## Which file do I download?

| You want... | Download |
| --- | --- |
| A normal install on Windows (Start Menu shortcut, uninstaller) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.19-windows-x64-setup.exe` |
| Windows without installing anything (unzip and run) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.19-windows-x64-portable.zip` |
| Linux: Fedora, Nobara, openSUSE (`dnf`/`zypper`) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.19-linux-x86_64.rpm` |
| Linux: Debian, Ubuntu, Mint (`apt`) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.19-linux-amd64.deb` |
| Linux: other distros, no install (uses your desktop's graphics libraries) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.19-linux-x86_64.AppImage` |
| Linux: Arch/CachyOS, or just the binary (needs WebKitGTK 4.1) | `DDMM-2.0.0-rc.19-linux-x64.tar.gz` |

Linux install commands, the dependencies for each distro, and fixes for a blank window or AppImage/FUSE errors
are in [Installing on Linux](https://katsyk.github.io/DemocracyDefenderModManager/getting-started/linux/).

**One-click install (optional):** also grab the browser extension: `ddmm-extension-chrome-1.0.1.zip`
(Chrome, Edge, Brave) or `ddmm-extension-firefox-1.0.1.zip` (Firefox). See
[One-click install](https://katsyk.github.io/DemocracyDefenderModManager/using/one-click-install/).

Check `SHA256SUMS.txt` if you want to verify your download.

## What's new in 2.0.0-rc.19

### Load order

- **Clearer names in each mod's three-dot menu:** "To Top" and "To Bottom" are now **Move to Top (lowest
  priority)** and **Move to Bottom (highest priority)**. The top of the list loads first, and the bottom wins
  conflicts.
- **"Mod not found" entries** have Move to Top and Move to Bottom too, since they keep their place in the load
  order.
- **With a search active,** Move to Top and Move to Bottom move the mod to the top or bottom of the *whole* list,
  counting the mods the search hides. If the search hides any mods, a short message tells you so.
- **With a search active,** Move Up and Move Down now move the mod past the next mod shown above or below it.
  Before, they could swap it with a hidden mod, so nothing seemed to happen. Without a search, they work as
  before.

As before, the new order reaches the game on your next Deploy. See
[Load order and conflicts](https://katsyk.github.io/DemocracyDefenderModManager/using/profiles/#load-order-and-conflicts).

### Keyboard

- **Escape closes the top popup** by choosing its safe answer: **No** on a confirmation, **Cancel** on
  "Replace?" (the installed mod is kept), **Deny** on the browser extension's consent question, and **OK** on
  results. One press closes one popup.
- **Escape does nothing** while something is in progress (deploying, importing, downloading and so on), on the
  import checklist (so your ticks stay), or on mod options.
- **The three-dot menu works from the keyboard:** it opens with focus on the first item, the arrow keys and
  Home/End move between items, and Escape closes it. Screen readers announce it as the actions for that mod.

### Import

When you import mods, or add 10 or more files at once, a file with the ID of a mod you already have can now
**replace** that mod from the checklist. Before, you had to add the file on its own to get the Replace question.

- It's shown as *Has the ID of "…" in DDMM: can replace it*, with both names and versions, a warning when the
  names differ, and a **Downgrade** label when the file is older than the installed mod.
- **It's never ticked for you,** not by default, not by **Only New** and not by **Select All**. Tick each one you
  want to replace.
- **One file per mod:** ticking a second file for the same mod unticks the first.
- **It uses the same Replace as rc.16:** the mod keeps its place in your profiles, whether it's on, and the
  option choices that still fit. If it's on in your active profile, DDMM redeploys once at the end (or asks to).
- **Identical files and mods you added by hand** still just get their Nexus info linked, as before. Only
  archives can replace; a mod folder with the same ID can't.
- **Cancel** can't undo a replace: mods replaced before you pressed Cancel stay replaced, and the summary says so.

See
[Replacing mods you already have](https://katsyk.github.io/DemocracyDefenderModManager/using/importing-mods/#replacing-mods-you-already-have).

### Maintenance

- **Updated a few libraries for security advisories** (rustix, quinn-proto and quinn-udp). None of them affect
  DDMM in practice, and the last two aren't even built into it.

### If you're coming from rc.14 or earlier

If you used the Skip List with rc.14 or earlier, verify the game files in Steam once (Library → Helldivers 2 →
Properties → Installed Files → Verify integrity of game files). Older versions could delete the game's own files
for those names.

**Skipped a few?** rc.10 had important safety fixes, rc.11 fixed mod deletion, rc.12 fixed mod option dropdowns, rc.13 fixed AyakaMods update checks, rc.14 fixed the Mods page stuck on "Loading...", rc.15 fixed Deploy and Purge removing mods and game files, rc.16 added Replace for mods with the same ID, rc.17 was a security update for archive extraction and rc.18 fixed a rare memory bug on Linux; see the [releases page](https://github.com/katsyk/DemocracyDefenderModManager/releases).

Thanks to everyone testing the release candidates. o7

## Known limitations

- **Windows builds are unsigned.** Windows SmartScreen will likely show a warning the first time you run the
  installer or the app. Click **"More info" → "Run anyway"** to continue.
- **The Linux .rpm and .deb are unsigned**, so openSUSE needs `zypper install --allow-unsigned-rpm`.
- **This is still a release candidate.** Expect some rough edges, and please report what you find.
